key_insight: Polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation reveals hidden, giant circular dichroism in chiral 2D perovskites, enabling telecom-band CPL detection with opposite chiral responses separated by output polarization.
engineering_relevance: This provides a route to compact, wavelength-telecom chiral photodetectors and polarization-encoded photonic devices for optical information processing, encryption, and anti-counterfeiting.
method: Measured third-harmonic generation circular dichroism (THG-CD) in chiral (R/S-MBACl)2PbI4.
Used polarization-resolved THG to separate orthogonal emission channels.
Compared chiral responses in total THG vs resolved channels to expose hidden anisotropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exceptionally large dissymmetry factors exceeding 1.9 when hidden polarization-resolved contributions are separated, far larger than conventional total-THG evaluation suggests.
watch_item: Device performance may be underestimated without polarization-resolved readout, so practical implementations need careful optical alignment and full vector-channel characterization.
paper_title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite
